title: The Light Came into the Darkness
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Jesus is God, eternal, the giver of life, and the light that came into our darkness. The darkness could not overcome him.
exhortation: "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one." One God, and Jesus was there in the beginning. If Jesus is not God, we are of all people most to be pitied. Christianity does not work without Jesus as God. And what a comfort John gives us here: an unequivocal, clear statement that Jesus is God. He was with God, eternal. He always was. There was never a time when he was not. We worship an eternal, awesome Savior.

Second, "in him was life." We learn in Colossians that all things were created through Jesus. His power was at work at creation, and from our first breath as humans, when Adam first breathed life into his lungs, it was Jesus giving him life. He gives us life today. His life-giving work has not stopped.

And finally, the light has come into the darkness. What a contrast: the God who always existed became a man. We're about to celebrate Christmas, and what a wonder it is that Jesus would humble himself. Our world is the darkness he came into. Jesus stepped into that darkness, and the darkness could not overcome him. Jesus conquered. He is the victor over darkness. That is the glorious Savior we worship this morning.
prayer: Jesus, you are from eternity. You are God. Instead of destroying a world that rebelled against you and cursed your name, you came into our darkness and bore our shame, guilt and sin so that we might be restored and saved. Thank you for piercing the darkness, for laying aside your glory and coming into our darkness.

As we face this day and whatever darkness is in it, be with us. Whatever happens today, in the elections, at work or in our relationships, remind us that you have overcome the world and that you reign over all. In your precious name, Jesus, amen.
